definition: Every planet moves in an elliptical orbit with the Sun at one focus of the ellipse.
The line joining the Sun and a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times, so the planet moves fastest when it is closest to the Sun.
For bodies orbiting the same central mass, the square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the mean orbital radius: $T^{2} \propto r^{3}$.
Two point masses attract each other with a force $F = G\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^{2}}$ along the line joining them, where $r$ is the distance between their centres.
A body modelled as all its mass at a single point; a uniform sphere acts as one at its centre for points on or outside its surface, and so does any body far away compared with its size.
The point at which the whole mass of a body can be taken to act; for a uniform sphere it is the centre.
The gravitational force per unit mass on a small point mass placed at a point, $g = \frac{F}{m}$, in $\text{N kg}^{-1}$; it points towards the mass causing the field.
